Evelyn / team — quick legal read of the redline PDF and spreadsheet. High-level: we can accept most of the language with a handful of carveouts and a proposed sequencing approach. Notes below (I'll prepare a marked-up DPA for the call):

1) Controller/Processor table: include a short exhibit that maps product features to data flows (we already have a template). Suggest: Redwood = processor (inference, embeddings, logs for X days), VelaMed = controller for customer-provided data. Laura — can you confirm retention buckets (logs vs. KV cache)?

2) EU SCCs: accept with processor Annex. For non-EEA routing: recommend SCCs + TIA. The TIA should be limited in scope (route patterns, kms key residency, mitigations).

3) Liability & data breach: VelaMed redline on liability cap tied to hosting jurisdiction — we should hold to the original MSA cap but offer a carveout for wilful misconduct and willful breach of security obligations.

4) Subprocessor notice: VelaMed asks for 30 days' notice; we typically provide 10 days' notice for critical subprocessors and a quarterly listing otherwise. Propose: 30-day notice for new subprocessor that will process EU data; otherwise quarterly disclosure.

5) Evidence index: we can produce a short technical binder (dscp_evidence_index.csv) covering encryption, key management (we operate HSM-backed KMS for hosted and dedicated; for private we support customer-managed keys), audit logs retention window, KV cache TTL default. Aditya — please populate the CSV with exact retention numbers and region routing details.

6) TIA sequencing: propose we (a) accept SCCs with redline exceptions flagged, (b) agree TIA template limited to routing and mitigations, (c) operationalize evidence delivery via a shared Drive link and a one-off tech attestation call.

I’ll produce a legal-marked DPA to circulate before Thu call.

—Ben
